organizations.name: United States Space Force
organizations.portfolio: Organize, train and equip space forces; owns the RDT&E Space Force, Procurement Space Force and O&M Space Force appropriations. Provides forces to USSPACECOM and other combatant commands through service components (e.g., Space Forces-Space).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Active. FY27 request sharply increases Space Force RDT&E (reported ~$38.4B, +159%, driven by Golden Dome and the new Space Data Network; Tier 3/4 reporting, Apr 2026). 2026 acquisition overhaul replaced program executive offices with nine Portfolio Acquisition Executives (PAEs) (DefenseScoop 2026-03-18; SpaceNews / Air & Space Forces mid-2026).
organizations.leader_title: Chief of Space Operations (CSO); Secretary of the Air Force is the civilian head. Space acquisition executive is the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Space Acquisition and Integration (SAF/SQ).
organizations.startup_relevance: The service is the budget owner; startups never contract with 'the Space Force' directly but with SSC/SDA/Space RCO/SpaceWERX contracting activities under the PAEs.

organizations.name: Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Space Acquisition and Integration
organizations.portfolio: Service Acquisition Executive for space; approves acquisition strategies, milestone decisions, and (in 2026) the sorting of programs into PAE portfolios. Ainsworth (title not re-verified this session) told reporters in May 2026 that DAF was 'still working' to sort space programs into portfolios.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Active; overseeing the PAE transition. INFERENCE: Because ~90-92% of contracting authority was reportedly delegated to PAEs, SAF/SQ is less a day-to-day gate for small prototype awards than before.
organizations.leader_title: Assistant Secretary of the Air Force (Space Acquisition and Integration) / acting officials in 2025-2026 (name not re-verified this session)
organizations.startup_relevance: Indirect: sets policy (e.g., commercial-first guidance, CSO usage) but is not a contracting office.

organizations.name: Space Systems Command
organizations.portfolio: Principal acquisition field command (Los Angeles AFB, CA) for satellites, ground systems, launch and C2/BMC3 software. Historically organized as five PEOs (Assured Access to Space; BMC3; Space Domain Awareness & Combat Power; MilComm & PNT; Space Sensing) plus System Deltas paired with SpOC Integrated Mission Deltas.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: In 2026 the Space Force replaced PEOs with nine PAEs: infrastructure; BMC3 and space intelligence (BMC3I); SATCOM and PNT; missile warning and tracking; space-based sensing and targeting; space access; electromagnetic warfare and cyber; space combat power; advanced capabilities. Final three PAEs were to stand up in the 'June-ish' 2026 timeframe (Breaking Defense 2026-04). SDA and Space RCO continue to exist but sit under the applicable PAE.
organizations.leader_title: Commander, Space Systems Command (Lieutenant General); PAEs are civilian SES or general-officer portfolio executives
key_programs: Space Data Network (portfolio assignment not verified)
organizations.startup_relevance: Primary buyer of C2/SDA software. Uses Commercial Solutions Openings (CSOs), OTAs (Space Enterprise Consortium), SBIR Phase III and FAR contracts. Runs a Commercial Space Office ('Front Door') for industry entry.

organizations.name: Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Battle Management, Command, Control, Communications and Space Intelligence
organizations.portfolio: Space command and control (ATLAS/Space C2), Kronos family of systems (C2, battle management, space intelligence), Unified Data Library, Warp Core data services, space-domain-awareness data/network modernization (SDANet), and related BMC3 ground software. SSC's public BMC3I page and fact sheet describe the mission.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Shannon Pallone, previously PEO for BMC3I, is now the permanent PAE for BMC3I (SSC leadership page; Breaking Defense 2026-05). FACT: 'Space Intelligence' was added to the portfolio name (BMC3 -> BMC3I) before the 2026 PAE conversion (SSC program office page).
organizations.startup_relevance: The single most relevant office for a C2/SDA software startup: it ran the Kronos CSO whose first awards (Apr 2026) were sub-$1.5M prototypes to a small firm (MapLarge) and a large one (Leidos), and later added True Anomaly's Mosaic.

organizations.name: Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Missile Warning and Tracking
organizations.parent: Space Systems Command / Space Force acquisition enterprise
organizations.portfolio: Missile warning/tracking constellations including SDA's Tracking Layer and legacy/next-gen OPIR elements; SDA director Gurpartap Sandhoo was appointed PAE for missile warning and tracking (2026).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Newly created in 2026 PAE overhaul; the SDA director dual-hats as PAE (ExecutiveGov / SpaceNews 2026). HYPOTHESIS: SDA's institutional identity may be absorbed into this PAE over time (National Defense Magazine 2026-08-03 discusses 'potential dissolution').
organizations.leader_title: Portfolio Acquisition Executive (Gurpartap Sandhoo, also Director SDA)
organizations.startup_relevance: Sensor-heavy portfolio; software openings are mainly BMC3/mission processing via SDA BAAs rather than direct C2 software buys.

organizations.name: Space Development Agency
organizations.parent: U.S. Space Force (since Oct 2022); in 2026 aligned under the applicable PAE
organizations.portfolio: Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture (PWSA): Transport Layer (Tranche 0/1/2 launched or in production), Tracking Layer (Tranche 3 awarded Dec 2025), BMC3 layer (on-orbit compute plus BMC3 Application Factory run by SAIC), ground/ops centers. Uses OTAs and BAAs heavily.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Tranche 3 Transport Layer was not funded in the FY27 request; requirements 'rolled into' the new Space Data Network backbone (DefenseScoop 2026-04-28; Breaking Defense 2026-04). FACT: SDA continues to exist under a PAE (Breaking Defense 2026-04). HYPOTHESIS (Tier 3, 2026-08-03): SDA could be dissolved as its functions migrate to PAEs; confidence LOW on timing.
organizations.leader_title: Director, SDA (Gurpartap Sandhoo, dual-hatted PAE MW&T)
organizations.startup_relevance: Historically the most open Space Force buyer of containerized mission software (BMC3 apps BAA). Transport-layer prime opportunities are now closed for startups; app-layer and ground-processing openings remain but are shrinking with T3 transport cancellation.

organizations.name: Space Rapid Capabilities Office
organizations.parent: U.S. Space Force (Kirtland AFB, NM); in 2026 under applicable PAE
organizations.portfolio: Rapid, often classified, space combat capabilities and the Rapid Resilient Command and Control (R2C2) cloud-based satellite C2 ground system for dynamic space operations.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: Continues to exist under a PAE after 2026 overhaul (Breaking Defense 2026-04). R2C2 IDIQ (est. $1B ceiling, 5-7 years) awarded June 2024 to 20 small businesses; first $12M in delivery orders Sept 26, 2024 (up to $600K each). DefenseScoop (2025-03-06) reported challenges scaling R2C2.
organizations.startup_relevance: R2C2 is small-business reserved (FACT) and agile/DevSecOps oriented; however the 20-vendor pool is closed unless an on-ramp is issued (not found this session). Anduril/Palantir are NOT R2C2 awardees (they are not small businesses); their Space Force C2-adjacent work is SDANet (Anduril) and Warp Core (Palantir).

organizations.name: SpaceWERX
organizations.parent: AFWERX (Air Force Research Laboratory) / Space Force innovation arm
organizations.portfolio: SBIR/STTR open topics, Direct-to-Phase-II, STRATFI/TACFI bridge funding, Orbital Prime (ISAM, $141M seeded since 2023), Tactically Responsive Space (TacRS) challenge with Space Safari, mission-focused cohorts tied to PAE/COCOM priorities.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: 2026 STRATFI cycle totaled $562.5M (SpaceWERX + program office + private capital; $245M private match) per Payload. FACT: Gravitics received a $60M STRATFI (PY 2025.1) for a TacRS orbital carrier (SpaceNews / Gravitics).
organizations.startup_relevance: Most realistic first-dollar path for a two-founder company IF SBIR ownership rules are met; program-office matching for STRATFI requires a sponsoring PAE customer.

organizations.name: SSC Commercial Space Office ('Front Door')
organizations.portfolio: Industry entry point for SSC; manages commercial integration efforts including the Commercial Augmentation Space Reserve (CASR) and, historically, Tactical Surveillance, Reconnaissance and Tracking (TacSRT) commercial data buys via the Global Data Marketplace (RECALL - not re-verified this session).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: CASR is moving out of pilot with next contracts planned in 2026 (Air & Space Forces Magazine). RECALL (MEDIUM): COMSO 'Front Door' remains the advertised submission portal for unsolicited capability briefs.
organizations.startup_relevance: Low-cost intake channel: submit a capability brief, get routed to a PAE; also the office that runs commercial-data purchase pilots where a data/analytics startup can sell directly.

organizations.name: Space Operations Command
organizations.parent: U.S. Space Force (field command, Peterson SFB, CO)
organizations.portfolio: Generates and presents space forces; Deltas include Delta 2 (space domain awareness; 18th/19th Space Defense Squadrons), Delta 3 (EW), Delta 4 (missile warning), Delta 5 (C2 / operations center support), Delta 6 (cyber and network ops), Delta 7 (ISR), Delta 8 (SATCOM/PNT), Delta 9 (orbital warfare), Delta 15 (NSDC support). Hosts the Joint Commercial Operations (JCO) cell that buys commercial SDA data on 4-6 week rolling contracts.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: In Sept 2025 SpOC explored reorganizing the commercial cell to push commercial monitoring data into operations (Breaking Defense 2025-09). RECALL (MEDIUM): Integrated Mission Deltas pair SpOC deltas with SSC System Deltas so operators and acquirers sit under one commander for sustainment.
organizations.startup_relevance: Source of operator pull; JCO rolling contracts are the fastest known direct-sale path for SDA data/analytics; delta-level CRADAs and user feedback are how requirements form.

organizations.name: Space Forces-Space
organizations.parent: U.S. Space Force service component to USSPACECOM (Vandenberg SFB, CA)
organizations.portfolio: Operates the Combined Space Operations Center (CSpOC) and, with USSPACECOM, the National Space Defense Center (NSDC); primary operational users of the space COP, ATLAS/SPADOC catalog, and Kronos battle-management tools. RECALL (MEDIUM): Joint Task Force-Space Defense functions were consolidated into S4S/NSDC around 2024-2025.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): S4S is the operational sponsor cited in Kronos and ATLAS coverage; Space Operations Command prepared a new shared domain-awareness tool for operators in late 2024 (Defense News 2024-12-23).
organizations.startup_relevance: Operational sponsor whose gaps drive SSC BMC3I CSOs; startups reach them via SSC industry days, JCO, and TEMs rather than direct sales.

organizations.name: United States Space Command
organizations.portfolio: Operational requirements for space domain awareness, space C2, and network modernization; e.g., mandated full deployment of the modernized Space Surveillance Network communications (SDANet) by end of 2026.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): USSPACECOM mandate on SDANet deployment by end-2026 reported May 2026. RECALL (LOW): HQ relocation to Huntsville, AL was ordered in 2025; status of move not verified this session.
organizations.startup_relevance: Requirement owner, not a buyer; influences urgency (e.g., ATLAS/SPADOC decommission, Kronos MVCs).

organizations.name: National Space Intelligence Center (Space Delta 18)
organizations.portfolio: Space intelligence production; its analysts are the intended users of Kronos 'space intelligence' capabilities (continuous adversary monitoring, multi-source data integration).
organizations.current_status_2026: RECALL (MEDIUM): Established June 2022; active. INFERENCE: Kronos's 'space intelligence' segment (SSC newsroom 2026-04) ties NSIC/Delta 7 analysts to BMC3I acquisition.
organizations.startup_relevance: Highly classified user base; startups without cleared staff can only reach it through cleared primes or unclassified data-layer work.

organizations.name: Space Training and Readiness Command
organizations.portfolio: Training, test (Delta 12), ranges/aggressors (Delta 11), doctrine; users of mission rehearsal and simulation tools.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): Slingshot Aerospace won a $69.2M Space Force contract (July 2026) for MENTAT, an AI mission-rehearsal platform; contracting office not verified.
key_programs: National Space Test and Training Complex
organizations.startup_relevance: Simulation/digital-twin and training software is a lower-classification entry point; Slingshot precedent shows scale is possible.

organizations.name: Air Force Research Laboratory Space Vehicles Directorate
organizations.parent: AFRL (Kirtland AFB, NM); supports Space Force S&T
organizations.portfolio: Space S&T including autonomy, SDA algorithms, resilient comms; funded under PE 1206310SF (Space Science and Technology R&D, $314M requested FY27 per Air & Space Forces Magazine).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: PE 1206310SF shows $314M in FY27 request (Tier 3). RECALL (MEDIUM): AFRL/RV runs BAAs and CRADAs open to small firms.
organizations.startup_relevance: CRADA/BAA sponsor and SBIR technical point of contact; useful for algorithm validation before a PAE buys.

organizations.name: Defense Innovation Unit - Space Portfolio
organizations.parent: Office of the Secretary of Defense
organizations.portfolio: Commercial Solutions Openings for space (e.g., Hybrid Space Architecture, commercial SDA, tactically responsive launch) with Space Force transition partners.
organizations.current_status_2026: RECALL (MEDIUM): Active; DIU CSO space projects typically pair with SSC or SpOC transition partners. Not re-verified this session.
organizations.startup_relevance: Non-SBIR path open to firms with foreign ownership (subject to FOCI/ITAR review); 24-month prototype OTs with follow-on production OT possible.

organizations.name: Space Enterprise Consortium (OTA)
organizations.portfolio: Section 4022 prototype OTA consortium used by SSC and other DoD space buyers for prototype projects; members include primes and nontraditionals. RECALL (MEDIUM): ceiling raised to ~$12B in 2020.
organizations.current_status_2026: RECALL (MEDIUM): Active; not re-verified this session. Public evidence insufficient on 2026 ceiling/usage.
key_programs: Prototype OT projects for SSC portfolios
organizations.startup_relevance: Membership fee and a US presence get a startup on the distribution for RFPs; realistic for $1-10M prototypes once a PAE sponsor exists.

organizations.name: Space Futures Command / Space Warfighting Analysis Center
organizations.parent: U.S. Space Force (planned fourth field command)
organizations.portfolio: Force design, concept development, wargaming; SWAC produces force designs (e.g., missile warning/tracking, SDA) that shape PAE portfolios.
organizations.current_status_2026: RECALL (LOW): Announced 2024 as a planned field command; stand-up status in 2026 not verified this session. Public evidence insufficient.
organizations.startup_relevance: Modeling/simulation and analytic tools; influence on requirements rather than purchases.

organizations.name: Office of Space Commerce (Dept. of Commerce) - TraCSS
organizations.portfolio: Civil space traffic coordination system (TraCSS) meant to take over civil conjunction warnings from DoD; pathfinder with LeoLabs, Slingshot, COMSPOC (Jan 2024).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): Sept 2026 reporting describes a DoD/industry 'showdown' over TraCSS's future, creating uncertainty about which agency buys commercial SSA data (Breaking Defense 2026-09).
organizations.startup_relevance: Adjacent civil buyer for the same SSA data/analytics; policy uncertainty is a demand risk for commercial-SDA startups.

programs.name: Space Command and Control (Space C2) / Advanced Tracking and Launch Analysis System (ATLAS) - 'Kobayashi Maru'
programs.owner: SSC PAE BMC3I (Space C2 software factory in Colorado Springs; program restructured FY2022)
programs.description: Replaces the 1980s Space Defense Operations Center (SPADOC) for catalog maintenance, conjunction/launch analysis and the space COP. ATLAS is the SPADOC-replacement baseline; the broader Space C2 effort delivers apps for operators at CSpOC/NSDC/Delta 2.
programs.status_2026: FACT: ATLAS achieved operational acceptance late 2025, but DOT&E's FY25 report (reported 2026-03) found it lacks minimum viable capability to decommission SPADOC, citing 'deficiencies consistent with system immaturity'. Officials plan SPADOC decommission by end of 2026 contingent on L3Harris 'astrometric tools' under a $90M contract awarded March 2025. Kronos was split out of Space C2 in May 2025.
vendors: Various software-factory support contractors (public evidence insufficient)

contract_evidence.vehicle: Contract for follow-on astrometric tools (vehicle type not verified)
contract_evidence.prototype_or_production: Production/sustainment enhancement of an operational system

budget.pe_number_or_line: Space Force RDT&E 'Space Command and Control' line historically (PE number not re-verified this session; verify in FY27 RDT&E Space Force J-book Vol 3). Related: PE 1206425SF Space Situation Awareness Systems (RECALL MEDIUM).
budget.fy27_request: Public evidence insufficient this session (FY27 J-books posted at af.mil SAF/FM Budget-2027 page).

programs.third_party_software_openness: INFERENCE: Space C2 was conceived as an app-based ecosystem with a software factory, and the 2025 split of Kronos (procured via CSO) indicates the government is deliberately opening the battle-management/intel layer to commercial software; ATLAS itself remains L3Harris-integrated. Confidence MEDIUM.

programs.name: Kronos Family of Systems
programs.description: Integrated family of systems consolidating legacy tools for operational C2, battle management and space intelligence; first minimum viable capability is a tool connecting planning, live operations and post-mission analysis with continuous adversary monitoring.
programs.status_2026: FACT: Planning began May 2025 when SSC separated Kronos from Space C2; SSC announced first CSO prototype awards on 2026-04-22 (Leidos $1.43M; MapLarge $499,828). FACT (Tier 3): True Anomaly later selected under a CSO award to provide its Mosaic software (Military Aerospace). A 'Kronos Family of Systems Commercial Solutions Opening' is posted on sam.gov (via third-party mirror).

budget.pe_number_or_line: Funded from the Space C2 / BMC3 RDT&E lines (specific PE not verified this session)

programs.third_party_software_openness: FACT: Procured through a CSO explicitly seeking commercial software with sub-$1.5M initial prototypes and multiple awardees including a small firm; HIGH openness relative to any other Space Force C2 program. Follow-on scale depends on prototype success (do not equate CSO award with production).

programs.name: Unified Data Library (UDL)
programs.owner: SSC PAE BMC3I (contractor Bluestaq, Colorado Springs)
programs.description: Cloud data library aggregating government and commercial space-object and SDA data across classification levels with public REST APIs; the de facto integration point for commercial SDA providers and for allied partners (Australia deployed a classified UDL instance).
programs.status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): Breaking Defense (2025-03) reported a 'multi-front push to fix' the UDL (performance/latency, governance). RECALL (MEDIUM): Bluestaq received a $280M Space Force contract to expand the UDL (SpaceNews, announced March 23; year believed 2023). FACT (Tier 3): Australian Defence contracted Bluestaq for a classified UDL rollout (iTnews).

contract_evidence.vehicle: Space Force contract (SBIR Phase III lineage, vehicle type not verified)
contract_evidence.awarded_value: $280M ceiling-type figure; do not equate with revenue

budget.pe_number_or_line: Within BMC3I/Space C2 RDT&E lines (PE not verified)

programs.third_party_software_openness: FACT: UDL exposes documented APIs (unifieddatalibrary.com) and Bluestaq publishes Python packages on PyPI; commercial providers can be onboarded as data producers/consumers. HIGH openness for data integration; the platform itself is single-vendor.

programs.name: Warp Core (data-as-a-service)
programs.description: Palantir-provided common data interface enabling data sharing, streamlining manual reporting and decommissioning legacy systems across SSC/Space Force.
programs.status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): SpaceNews reported the Space Force extended Palantir's data-as-a-service contracts (date not re-verified). No 2026 award found this session.
programs.third_party_software_openness: INFERENCE: A Palantir-hosted data layer tends to lock third parties into Palantir's integration patterns; startups more commonly integrate via UDL. Confidence MEDIUM.

programs.name: Space Surveillance Network modernization - SDANet (mesh networking)
programs.owner: SSC (portfolio: space domain awareness; PAE assignment not verified)
programs.description: Next-generation resilient communications architecture replacing fragmented legacy links among Space Surveillance Network sensors; built on Anduril's Lattice-class mesh networking.
programs.status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): Anduril received $99.7M in Nov 2024 and a $100.3M modification on 2026-05-05 raising the ceiling to $200M; USSPACECOM mandates full deployment by end of 2026.

contract_evidence.vehicle: Contract modification (base vehicle type not verified)

budget.pe_number_or_line: Likely PE 1206425SF Space Situation Awareness Systems (RECALL, MEDIUM; not verified)

programs.third_party_software_openness: INFERENCE: Vendor-owned mesh (Lattice) with government-mandated interfaces; third-party sensor/analytics integration likely via Anduril SDK or UDL. Confidence LOW.

programs.name: SDA Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture - Transport Layer (Tranche 0/1/2) and BMC3 layer
programs.owner: Space Development Agency (under PAE structure since 2026)
programs.description: LEO mesh of optically linked satellites carrying Link 16, IBS and tactical data (JADC2 'space transport layer'); BMC3 modules provide on-orbit processing; SAIC runs the BMC3 Application Factory; SDA BAAs solicit containerized battle-management mission applications.
programs.status_2026: FACT: Tranche 3 Transport Layer not funded in FY27; requirements shifted to the Space Data Network backbone. FACT (Tier 3): Tranche 1 and 2 received a combined $817M RDT&E in FY27 request. RECALL (MEDIUM): T2 transport vendors York (~$615M, Aug 2022), Northrop (~$692M, Aug 2022), Lockheed (~$816M, Aug 2023), Rocket Lab (~$515M, Jan 2024).
vendors: Scientific Systems Company (T1 BMC3 software, RECALL LOW)
Raytheon (T1 Tracking, RECALL MEDIUM; not BMC3)
Anduril (no SDA/PWSA award found this session)

contract_evidence.vehicle: Other Transaction agreement - BMC3 Application Factory and middleware
Broad Agency Announcement for PWSA Battle Management Mission Applications (white papers then invited proposals)

budget.pe_number_or_line: Transport Layer historically funded partly via PE 1206310SF (Space S&T R&D; $314M FY27) and PE 1206410SF (Space Technology Development and Prototyping; $1.25B FY27) plus SDA tranche lines (T1+T2 $817M FY27). Exact SDA PE numbers not re-verified.
budget.fy26_request: Public evidence insufficient this session (Congress reinstated $500M for T3 transport in FY26 per Breaking Defense).

programs.third_party_software_openness: FACT: BMC3 layer was deliberately designed for containerized third-party apps via an Application Factory and BAA; openness HIGH in design, but with T3 transport cancelled and SDA's future uncertain, the funded pipeline for new apps is uncertain (INFERENCE, MEDIUM).

programs.name: Space Data Network (SDN)
programs.owner: Space Force (portfolio assignment not verified; likely BMC3I or SATCOM & PNT PAE - INFERENCE LOW)
programs.description: New FY27 multi-billion 'backbone' for orbital data relay intended to absorb Tranche 3 Transport Layer requirements and connect sensing, missile-defense (Golden Dome) and tactical users.
programs.status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): Announced with the FY27 budget (DefenseScoop 2026-04-28; Breaking Defense 2026-04). FACT (Tier 3): Space Force awarded SpaceX a $2.3B contract for the SDN (Via Satellite 2026-05-27); Quilty commentary dubbed it the 'Space(x) Data Network'.

contract_evidence.awarded_value: $2.3B reported award value; treat as ceiling until obligations verified

budget.pe_number_or_line: New FY27 line(s); 'billions' planned (DefenseScoop); PE not verified
budget.fy27_request: Multi-billion (exact figure not verified this session)

programs.third_party_software_openness: HYPOTHESIS: A SpaceX-anchored backbone (Starshield lineage) will be less open to third-party on-orbit apps than SDA's BMC3 model; openings shift to ground/user terminals, crypto/waveform interop, and data services. Confidence LOW.

programs.name: SDA Tracking Layer Tranche 3 (context for sensing/targeting)
programs.owner: SDA / PAE Missile Warning and Tracking
programs.status_2026: FACT: Awarded 2025-12-19 (~$3.5B across four teams: Lockheed Martin, Rocket Lab, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris; 18 satellites each).

contract_evidence.vendor: Lockheed Martin / Rocket Lab / Northrop Grumman / L3Harris

budget.pe_number_or_line: SDA Tracking Layer lines (PE not verified)

programs.third_party_software_openness: LOW for startups at prime level; mission data processing subcontracts possible.

programs.name: Rapid Resilient Command and Control (R2C2)
programs.description: Cloud-based, DevSecOps satellite C2 ground system for 'dynamic space operations' (frequently maneuvering satellites); modular, incremental delivery via CI/CD.
programs.status_2026: FACT: IDIQ estimated at $1B over 5-7 years awarded June 2024 to 20 small businesses; first $12M in delivery orders 2024-09-26 (up to $600K each). FACT (Tier 3): DefenseScoop (2025-03-06) reported the Space Force is challenged to scale R2C2. 2026 status and vendor names not verified this session (egress-blocked).
vendors: 20 small businesses (names not verified this session - public evidence insufficient)

contract_evidence.awarded_value: Up to $600K per company in first orders

budget.pe_number_or_line: PE 1206857SF Space Rapid Capabilities Office (RECALL, MEDIUM; not verified)

programs.third_party_software_openness: FACT: Explicitly modular/agile and small-business-only; HIGH openness in principle but the awardee pool is closed; a new startup would need an on-ramp or a subcontract to a pool member.

programs.name: Commercial SDA integration: Joint Commercial Operations (JCO) cell, Commercial Augmentation Space Reserve (CASR), Commercial Space Strategy
programs.owner: SpOC (JCO) / SSC Commercial Space Office (CASR) / USSF HQ (strategy, April 2024)
programs.description: JCO buys commercial space-monitoring data/analytics on 4-6 week competitive rolling contracts with 'constant on-boarding' (vendors: LeoLabs, ExoAnalytic, Slingshot, COMSPOC). CASR is a Civil-Reserve-Air-Fleet-like pool of commercial capacity for crisis. The April 2024 Commercial Space Strategy names SDA, SATCOM, TacSRT and other mission areas for commercial integration (RECALL MEDIUM on contents).
programs.status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): CASR moving out of pilot with next contract batch planned 2026. FACT (Tier 3): Anduril announced acquisition of ExoAnalytic (2026-03-11). FACT (Tier 3): Slingshot won $69.2M for MENTAT (2026-07). Contract sizes for JCO buys not disclosed.

contract_evidence.vehicle: Space Force contract (vehicle not verified; MENTAT AI mission rehearsal)

budget.pe_number_or_line: Mixed O&M/RDT&E; JCO funding line not verified

programs.third_party_software_openness: HIGH: JCO's model is designed for constant onboarding of commercial providers; entry requires unique data or demonstrably better analytics, typically delivered into UDL.

programs.name: Andromeda (GEO reconnaissance/surveillance task-order program)
programs.description: 10-year, $1.8B multiple-award program to issue task orders to 14 space companies for GEO reconnaissance and surveillance missions; Anduril among awardees.
programs.status_2026: FACT (Tier 4, 2026-04-29): Reported by Motley Fool/Yahoo; 14 awardees; ceiling is not revenue. Other awardee names not verified this session.
programs.third_party_software_openness: LOW for a software-only startup (spacecraft-centric); subcontract for mission software possible.

programs.name: SpaceWERX Orbital Prime / Tactically Responsive Space (TacRS) / STRATFI 2026
programs.owner: SpaceWERX (AFWERX) with Space Safari and PAE sponsors
programs.description: SBIR-funded cohorts: Orbital Prime ($141M seeded since 2023 for ISAM), TacRS challenge (respond to on-orbit threats by 2026) and STRATFI/TACFI bridge funding.
programs.status_2026: FACT (Tier 3): 2026 STRATFI cycle $562.5M total with $245M private match (Payload). FACT: Gravitics $60M STRATFI (PY2025.1) for TacRS orbital carrier.
vendors: Other 2026 STRATFI awardees (list not retrieved - egress blocked)

contract_evidence.vehicle: STRATFI (SBIR Phase II bridge with program-office and private match)
contract_evidence.awarded_value: $60M follow-on investment (mix of SBIR, program office and private match)

budget.pe_number_or_line: SBIR/STTR set-aside across Space Force RDT&E plus matching program-office funds

programs.third_party_software_openness: HIGH for eligible small businesses; software topics compete against hardware-heavy space topics.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: SpaceWERX (AFWERX) runs Space Force SBIR/STTR open topics and mission-focused cohorts; Phase I feasibility, Phase II prototype, Phase III sole-source follow-on by any DoD office (Bluestaq's UDL is the canonical Phase III success).
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: Phase I roughly $75K-$150K; Phase II roughly $0.75M-$1.8M (RECALL MEDIUM)
procurement_pathways.timeline: Open-topic cycles 2-3x/year; ~3-6 months from submission to Phase I award; Phase II 12-24 months

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: Best first-dollar path if eligible; software topics welcomed; requires a Space Force customer memo for Phase II open topics.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: SBIR requires a for-profit US small business more than 50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents (a German permanent resident counts; an Indonesian non-US-person co-founder holding a large stake could break the >50% test); principal place of business and work in the US. Needs specialist review of the cap table before applying.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: AFWERX/SpaceWERX D2P2 open topics allow skipping Phase I with evidence of feasibility (e.g., a working product with commercial traction).

procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: TACFI up to ~$2M SBIR + match; STRATFI up to ~$15M SBIR + match (totals to $60M seen)

how_a_startup_gets_in: Sequenced plan for a two-founder, ~$250K company targeting Space Force C2/SDA software. (0) Legal first: get a cap-table and export-control review before anything else - SBIR requires >50% US-citizen/permanent-resident ownership (German LPR counts; Indonesian non-US-person stake must be sized accordingly), and space C2/SDA software can be ITAR-controlled; classified Kronos/NSDC work needs facility clearance and FOCI mitigation (specialist review, no legal judgment here). (1) Build on the Unified Data Library: register for UDL API access (unifieddatalibrary.com), ingest public/commercial catalog data and ship an unclassified analytic (e.g., maneuver detection, conjunction triage, sensor-tasking optimization) that demonstrates value in weeks; this is the integration layer every SSC/SpOC program uses. (2) Get operator pull: attend SSC BMC3I industry days and technical exchange meetings (SSC Space Industry Days, AFCEA LA), submit a capability brief through the SSC Commercial Space Office 'Front Door', and seek a no-cost CRADA or demo with Space Delta 2, the JCO cell, or AFRL/RV. (3) First dollars via SpaceWERX: submit to the next SpaceWERX/AFWERX open topic or 2026 challenge (afwerxchallenge.com/spacewerx26), ideally Direct-to-Phase-II with a customer memo from a delta or the BMC3I office; alternatively DIU Space CSO if SBIR-ineligible. (4) In parallel, sell commercially: onboard as a JCO commercial-data/analytics provider (4-6 week rolling competitions) and position for the 2026 CASR contract batch; consider allied buyers (Australia's classified UDL, German Weltraumkommando/GSSAC) where the German founder helps. (5) Target the Kronos Family of Systems CSO for a $0.5M-$1.5M prototype OT - the only Space Force C2 program in 2026 that awarded sub-$1M prototypes to small commercial software vendors - and/or the SDA BMC3 Battle Management mission-applications BAA while it lasts. (6) Team with primes and pool members: subcontract to Leidos/True Anomaly (Kronos), L3Harris (ATLAS), SAIC (BMC3 App Factory), Bluestaq (UDL), or an R2C2 small-business pool member; join the Space Enterprise Consortium (NSTXL) for RFP visibility. (7) Scale via STRATFI/TACFI (needs a PAE sponsor and private match) toward a Phase III or production OT. Avoid: pitching on-orbit transport (SDN is SpaceX-anchored), Golden Dome fire control (classified, prime-dominated), or hardware-heavy TacRS/ISAM cohorts.

saturation_statement: Coverage is strong on the 2026 acquisition reorganization (PAEs), Kronos, ATLAS/SPADOC status, SDA transport-to-SDN shift, R2C2 structure, SDANet, and commercial-SDA buying patterns, all with 2025-2026 sources. Gaps remaining after the 12-search budget: exact FY26/FY27 PE numbers and dollar figures for the Space C2/BMC3I lines (need FY27 RDT&E Space Force J-book, Vol 3), names of the 20 R2C2 awardees and any 2025-2026 on-ramp, the 2026 STRATFI awardee list, SDA BM mission-app BAA award recipients, BigBear.ai/Accelint/Kratos/Parsons Space Force C2 roles, and which PAE owns the Space Data Network and SDANet. Two WebFetch attempts to third-party sites were egress-blocked. Absence of found competitors in a niche is not evidence of opportunity; the SDA/space-C2 software niche is already contested by Slingshot, LeoLabs, COMSPOC, True Anomaly, MapLarge, Bluestaq, Palantir and Anduril (which now owns ExoAnalytic).
